title: Why I Started Walking Without My Phone
script: Narrator: [honestly] For a long time, my morning walks were not really walks. I looked at my phone the whole time, and I barely noticed the street around me.
Narrator: [thoughtful] I passed the same trees every day, but I could not have described them if someone asked me to.
Narrator: [reflective] One morning, my phone battery died before I left the house. I almost turned back to charge it, but I decided to walk anyway.
Narrator: [softly] Without the screen in my hand, I noticed the air first. It was cool, and it smelled like wet grass after the night's rain.
Narrator: [warmly] Then I noticed the trees. One had small yellow flowers I had never seen before, even though I passed it almost every day.
Narrator: [gently] Birds were singing loudly in the branches above me. I stopped for a moment and just listened, which felt strange at first.
Narrator: [thoughtful] I realized I had walked past this same park for two years without truly seeing it.
Narrator: [determined] So now, I leave my phone at home three mornings a week. It is a small change, but it feels important.
Narrator: [honestly] The first few walks felt boring without something to look at. My hands did not know what to do without a screen.
Narrator: [gently] But after a week, boredom turned into something else. I started noticing small changes, like new leaves or a different bird each morning.
Narrator: [peacefully] Now I know which trees flower first in spring, and which corner of the park stays shady even at noon.
Narrator: [reflective] My sister asked me why I bother, since nothing about the walk itself changed. But everything about how I experience it changed.
Narrator: [warmly] A slow walk with open eyes teaches you more than a fast walk with a screen ever could. That is what I learned this year.

quiz.question: How did the narrator usually spend her morning walks before this change?
options: Looking at her phone the whole time
quiz.explanation: She says her walks were not really walks because she looked at her phone the whole time.

quiz.question: What happened one morning that changed things?

quiz.explanation: Her phone battery died before she left the house, so she walked without it.

quiz.question: What did she notice first without her phone?
options: The cool air that smelled like wet grass
quiz.explanation: She says she noticed the cool air first, which smelled like wet grass after the night's rain.

quiz.question: What does the narrator do now, several times a week?
quiz.explanation: She now leaves her phone at home three mornings a week.

quiz.question: What is the narrator's final lesson?
options: Walking is a waste of time
A slow walk with open eyes teaches more than a fast walk with a screen
Phones should never be used outside
quiz.explanation: She concludes that a slow walk with open eyes teaches more than a fast walk with a screen.
